gap: No result ChatGPT got states a measured panel output. OutdoorGearLab (Sam Schild, updated 2026-07-13) measured the panels that come in the 200 W kits side by side on one clear day: EcoFlow NextGen 220W at 193 W (88%), Jackery SolarSaga 200 at 171 W, Anker SOLIX PS200 at 166 W and Bluetti 200W at 150 W (75%). Named reviewers measured 360 W from both 400 W panels in the shopper's top kits: ALLPOWERS SP037 (Beyond the Tent) and EcoFlow 400W (CleanTechnica).
standout_why: Trek4Tech (cited) says 'We did not test any of these units.' It applies one flat 0.65 derating to every panel: Anker C1000 + 200W, Bluetti AC180 + 200W, Jackery 1000 v2 + 200W, EcoFlow Delta 2 + 220W, Jackery 2000 v2 + 2x200W and River 2 Pro + 220W. RuntimeMath uses a flat 0.75 and says 'We don't test panels.' Popular Science (2026-11-05) gives only maker solar specs and no solar measurements. None of these pages has a measured watt figure for any bundled panel. OGL's measurements show the gap between brands is real: 88% for EcoFlow against 75% for Bluetti, and a flat derating hides that. I couldn't read TheOutagePlan (cited) because its SSL certificate failed, so I couldn't compare against it.
decides: It confirms that the panel size relative to the battery decides the pick, and that a 400 W kit beats any 200 W kit. Both 400 W panels in the shopper's shortlist were measured at about 360 W peak, so the ALLPOWERS P1800 + SP037 (1,024 Wh) and the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus + 400W (1,024 Wh) work out to about 2.8 h of full sun at that rate. The two are tied, so price decides it ($698 for the ALLPOWERS kit on iallpowers.com today). Among 200 W kits, the measurements reorder Trek4Tech's list. EcoFlow 1,024 Wh / 193 W comes to about 5.3 h. Jackery 1000 v2 1,070 Wh / 171 W is about 6.3 h. Anker C1000 1,024 Wh / 166 W is about 6.2 h. Bluetti AC180 1,152 Wh / 150 W is about 7.7 h, the slowest even though it has the biggest battery. Side note: ALLPOWERS also sells a P1800 + 600 W kit for $798, and the P1800 accepts up to 650 W, so that kit should refill faster than either 400 W kit. Nobody has measured it.
